claim: PIP5K family of lipid-modifying enzymes generate the majority of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate [PI(4,5)P2] lipids found at the plasma membrane in eukaryotic cells.
source: The phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate 5-kinase (PIP5K) family of lipid-modifying enzymes generate the majority of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate [PI(4,5)P2] lipids found at the plasma membrane in eukaryotic cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the function of PIP5K enzymes.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 lipids serve a critical role in regulating receptor activation, ion channel gating, endocytosis, and actin nucleation.
source: PI(4,5)P2 lipids serve a critical role in regulating receptor activation, ion channel gating, endocytosis, and actin nucleation.
evidence: This statement describes the biological functions of PI(4,5)P2 lipids based on established knowledge.

claim: Solution PIP5K exists in a weak monomer–dimer equilibrium, in contrast to constitutively dimeric PIP4K.
source: In contrast to constitutively dimeric phosphatidylinositol 5-phosphate 4-kinase (PIP4K, type II PIPK), solution PIP5K exists in a weak monomer–dimer equilibrium.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental observations.

claim: PIP5K monomers can associate with PI(4,5)P2-containing membranes and dimerize in a protein density-dependent manner.
source: PIP5K monomers can associate with PI(4,5)P2-containing membranes and dimerize in a protein density-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a primary finding describing the membrane-binding behavior of PIP5K.

claim: Dimerization enhances the catalytic efficiency of PIP5K through a mechanism consistent with allosteric regulation.
source: Although dispensable for cooperative PI(4,5)P2 binding, dimerization enhances the catalytic efficiency of PIP5K through a mechanism consistent with allosteric regulation.
evidence: This is a primary finding describing the effect of dimerization on PIP5K activity.

claim: Dimerization amplifies stochastic variation in the kinase reaction velocity.
source: Additionally, dimerization amplifies stochastic variation in the kinase reaction velocity and strengthens effects such as the recently described stochastic geometry sensing.
evidence: This is a primary finding describing the effect of dimerization on reaction kinetics.

claim: The mechanism of PIP5K membrane binding creates a broad dynamic range of lipid kinase activities that are coupled to the density of PI(4,5)P2 and membrane-bound kinase.
source: Overall, the mechanism of PIP5K membrane binding creates a broad dynamic range of lipid kinase activities that are coupled to the density of PI(4,5)P2 and membrane-bound kinase.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 comprises approximately 2% of the total cellular membrane composition.
source: Of particular importance to a vast array of signaling pathways are phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate [PI(4,5)P2] lipids, which comprise a minor phospholipid component of the total cellular membrane composition (i.e., ~2 %) (Wenk et al., 2003; Nasuhoglu et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 serves important functions in receptor activation, ion channel function, endocytosis, and actin network assembly at the plasma membrane.
source: PI(4,5)P2 serves many important functions in biological processes, including receptor activation, ion channel function (Hansen, 2015), endocytosis (Zoncu et al., 2007; Jost et al., 1998), and actin network assembly at the plasma membrane (Janmey et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Two classes of lipid kinases catalyze the production of PI(4,5)P2 lipids: PIP5K (type I PIPK) and PIP4K (type II PIPK).
source: Two classes of lipid kinases catalyze the production of PI(4,5)P2 lipids: phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate 5-kinase (PIP5K, type I PIPK) and phosphatidylinositol 5-phosphate 4-kinase (PIP4K, type II PIPK) (Burke, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: PIP5K phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI(4)P), while PIP4K phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol 5-phosphate (PI(5)P).
source: These two families of lipid kinases differ in substrate specificity; PIP5K phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate – PI(4)P, while PIP4K phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol 5-phosphate – PI(5)P (Loijens and Anderson, 1996; Rameh et al., 1997; Muftuoglu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The majority of PI(4,5)P2 lipids are generated from reactions catalyzed by PIP5K due to the higher abundance of PI(4)P in the plasma membrane relative to PI(5)P.
source: Due to the higher abundance of PI(4)P in the plasma membrane, relative to PI(5)P, the majority of PI(4,5)P2 lipids are generated from reactions catalyzed by PIP5K (Doughman et al., 2003; Balla, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Yeast express a single PIP5K enzyme denoted Mss4 (multicopy suppressor of Stt4).
source: Functionally conserved across eukaryotes, yeast express a single PIP5K enzyme denoted Mss4 (multicopy suppressor of Stt4) (Yoshida et al., 1994; Homma et al., 1998; Desrivières et al., 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In humans, three paralogs – PIP5KA, PIP5KB, and PIP5KC – regulate the production of most PI(4,5)P2 lipids found at the plasma membrane.
source: In humans, three paralogs – PIP5KA, PIP5KB, and PIP5KC – regulate the production of most PI(4,5)P2 lipids found at the plasma membrane.
evidence: This statement describes the human PIP5K paralogs based on established knowledge.

claim: Several mechanisms regulate membrane docking of PIP5K, including substrate recognition, electrostatic interactions with anionic lipids, and membrane binding of an amphipathic helix.
source: Several mechanisms regulate membrane docking of PIP5K, including substrate recognition (Muftuoglu et al., 2016; Kunz et al., 2000), electrostatic interactions with anionic lipids at the cell plasma membrane (Fairn et al., 2009), and membrane binding of an amphipathic helix (Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Single-molecule characterization of human PIP5KB has revealed a role for PI(4,5)P2 lipids in controlling cooperative membrane association and positive feedback during PI(4)P lipid phosphorylation reaction.
source: Single-molecule characterization of human PIP5KB has revealed a role for PI(4,5)P2 lipids in controlling cooperative membrane association and positive feedback during PI(4)P lipid phosphorylation reaction (Hansen et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Structural and biochemical studies indicate that PIP5K can homodimerize in solution, like PIP4K.
source: Structural and biochemical studies indicate that, like PIP4K (Rao et al., 1998; Burden et al., 1999), PIP5K can homodimerize in solution (Hu et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Dimerization of zebrafish PIP5KA has been shown to be required for lipid kinase activity.
source: In the case of zebrafish PIP5KA (zPIP5KA), dimerization has been shown to be required for lipid kinase activity (Hu et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: It remains unclear whether dimerization regulates membrane docking, ATP binding, or catalysis of PIP5K.
source: It remains unclear whether dimerization regulates membrane docking, ATP binding, or catalysis of PIP5K.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: Human PIP5KB catalyzes the phosphorylation of PI(4)P with a positive feedback loop based on association with its reaction product, PI(4,5)P2.
source: Using total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy to measure the kinetics of PIP lipid phosphorylation on supported lipid bilayers (SLBs) in vitro, we previously reported that human PIP5KB catalyzes the phosphorylation of PI(4)P with a positive feedback loop based on association with its reaction product, PI(4,5)P2 (Hansen et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Wild-type and the dimerization-deficient zebrafish PIP5KA (zPIP5KA) mutant, D84R, showed distinct SEC elution profiles that reflect the dimeric and monomeric states of each kinase.
source: Consistent with size-exclusion chromatography and multi-angle light scattering (SEC/MALS) data published by Hu et al., 2015, we found that wild-type and the dimerization-deficient zebrafish PIP5KA (zPIP5KA) mutant, D84R, showed distinct SEC elution profiles that reflect the dimeric and monomeric states of each kinase (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and is consistent with previous studies.

claim: zPIP5KA eluted slowly compared to PIP4KB and protein molecular weight standards, despite both being predicted to have dimeric molecular weights of 90 kDa.
source: However, comparing the SEC elution profiles of zPIP5KA and PIP4KB – both predicted to have dimeric molecular weights of 90 kDa – indicated that zPIP5KA eluted slowly compared to PIP4KB and protein molecular weight standards (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Differences in the elution profile of zPIP5KA and PIP4KB could be the result of distinct subunit orientations or the oligomerization state.
source: Differences in the elution profile of zPIP5KA and PIP4KB could be the result of distinct subunit orientations or the oligomerization state.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed SEC elution profiles.

claim: The majority of mNG-PIP4KB molecules were two times brighter compared to membrane-bound mNG-PIP5KB.
source: Intensity line scans through mNG foci revealed that the majority of mNG-PIP4KB molecules were two times brighter compared to membrane-bound mNG-PIP5KB (Figure 1C).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The vast majority of membrane-bound mNG-PIP4KB particles photobleached in two steps.
source: In the case of mNG-PIP4KB, the vast majority of membrane-bound particles photobleached in two steps (Figure 1D).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Single-membrane-bound mNG-PIP5KB particles photobleached in a single step.
source: By contrast, single-membrane-bound mNG-PIP5KB particles photobleached in a single step (Figure 1E).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Over the course of a 10 s photobleaching experiment, the molecular brightness distribution for mNG-PIP4KB shifted from bimodal to a single peak.
source: Over the course of a 10 s photobleaching experiment, the molecular brightness distribution for mNG-PIP4KB shifted from bimodal to a single peak (Figure 1F, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: During photobleaching, the fraction of mNG-PIP4KB dimers with two visible mNG fluorophores gradually decreased from ~80% to ~20% of the population.
source: During this time, the fraction of mNG-PIP4KB dimers with two visible mNG fluorophores gradually decreased from ~80% to ~20% of the population (Figure 1H).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The molecular brightness distribution of mNG-PIP5KB remained unimodal throughout the 10 s photobleaching experiment, consistent with mNG-PIP5KB associating with PI(4,5)P2-containing membranes predominantly as a monomer at a low protein surface density.
source: By contrast, the molecular brightness distribution of mNG-PIP5KB remained unimodal throughout the 10 s photobleaching experiment, consistent with mNG-PIP5KB associating with PI(4,5)P2-containing membranes predominantly as a monomer at a low protein surface density (Figure 1G, Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: At low surface densities (~0.01 molecules/µm2), the mobility of mNG-PIP4KB (0.04 µm2/s) was much slower compared to mNG-PIP5K homologs and paralogs (0.15–0.18 µm2/s).
source: At low surface densities (~0.01 molecules/µm2), the mobility of mNG-PIP4KB (0.04 µm2/s) was much slower compared to mNG-PIP5K homologs and paralogs (0.15–0.18 µm2/s) (Figure 1J).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: In the presence of a low density of noninteracting Ax647-PIP5KB monomers (i.e., 1–5 pM solution concentration), the distribution of single-molecule dwell times could be fit to a single exponential with a characteristic dwell time of ~0.45 s.
source: In the presence of a low density of noninteracting Ax647-PIP5KB monomers (i.e., 1–5 pM solution concentration), the distribution of single-molecule dwell times could be fit to a single exponential with a characteristic dwell time of ~0.45 s (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: When the solution concentration of dark unlabeled PIP5KB was increased, a second population of long dwelling Ax647-PIP5KB molecules was observed.
source: When we increased the solution concentration of dark unlabeled PIP5KB, we observed a second population of long dwelling Ax647-PIP5KB molecules (Figure 2B, Table 1, Figure 2—video 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Table 1.

claim: At concentrations greater than 1 nM dark unlabeled PIP5KB, the resulting dwell time distributions for Ax647-PIP5KB were best fit to a two-species model with two characteristic dwell times.
source: At concentrations greater than 1 nM dark unlabeled PIP5KB, the resulting dwell time distributions for Ax647-PIP5KB were best fit to a two-species model with two characteristic dwell times (Figure 2B, Table 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Table 1.

claim: A protein surface density-dependent decrease in the diffusion coefficient of membrane-bound Ax647-PIP5KB was observed.
source: In addition to observing an enhancement in the dwell time, we also observed a protein surface density-dependent decrease in the diffusion coefficient of membrane-bound Ax647-PIP5KB (Figure 2C, Table 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and Table 1.

claim: The density of membrane-bound Ax647-PIP5KB dramatically increased as a function of the PI(4,5)P2 density.
source: These measurements revealed two nonlinear membrane-binding behaviors of Ax647-PIP5KB. First, the density of membrane-bound Ax647-PIP5KB dramatically increased as a function of the PI(4,5)P2 density (Figure 2F).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Increasing the solution concentration promoted cooperative membrane binding of Ax647-PIP5KB based on elevated protein densities.
source: Second, increasing the solution concentration promoted cooperative membrane binding of Ax647-PIP5KB based on elevated protein densities (Figure 2F).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Fitting the membrane-binding curves with a concerted model for cooperativity yielded dissociation constants of 212 nM and 52 nM for Ax647-PIP5KB in the presence of 2% and 4% PI(4,5)P2 lipids, respectively.
source: Fitting the membrane-binding curves with a concerted model for cooperativity yielded dissociation constants of 212 nM and 52 nM for Ax647-PIP5KB in the presence of 2% and 4% PI(4,5)P2 lipids, respectively (Figure 2F).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data and curve fitting shown in Figure 2F.

claim: When measured at a low protein surface density (~0.01 molecule/µm2), the PIP5KB (D51R) mutant still bound cooperatively to PI(4,5)P2 lipids in a manner that was indistinguishable from the wild-type kinase.
source: When measured at a low protein surface density (~0.01 molecule/µm2), the PIP5KB (D51R) mutant still bound cooperatively to PI(4,5)P2 lipids in a manner that was indistinguishable from the wild-type kinase (Figure 3C and D, Table 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D, and Table 2.

claim: Under low protein density conditions, the diffusion coefficients of membrane-bound Ax647-PIP5KB and Ax647-PIP5KB (D51R) were indistinguishable.
source: Under these conditions, the diffusion coefficients of membrane-bound Ax647-PIP5KB and Ax647-PIP5KB (D51R) were indistinguishable (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Single-molecule membrane-binding experiments performed using a high kinase surface density (~100 molecules/µm2) revealed that the single-molecule dwell time of Ax647-PIP5KB increased, while the dwell time of the D51R mutant remained unchanged in the presence of 50 nM unlabeled PIP5KB.
source: In contrast, single-molecule membrane-binding experiments performed using a high kinase surface density (~100 molecules/µm2) revealed that the single-molecule dwell time of Ax647-PIP5KB increased, while the dwell time of the D51R mutant remained unchanged in the presence of 50 nM unlabeled PIP5KB (Figure 3E, Table 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E and Table 2.

claim: The diffusion coefficient of wild-type Ax647-PIP5KB decreased due to membrane-mediated dimerization, while diffusivity of Ax647-PIP5KB (D51R) remained unchanged in the presence of 50 nM dark PIP5KB.
source: In addition, the diffusion coefficient of wild-type Ax647-PIP5KB decreased due to membrane-mediated dimerization, while diffusivity of Ax647-PIP5KB (D51R) remained unchanged in the presence of 50 nM dark PIP5KB (Figure 3F).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Comparing the kinetics of PI(4,5)P2 production on SLBs in the presence of either PIP5KB and PIP5KB (D51R) revealed that dimerization enhances catalytic activity, but is not essential for generation of PI(4,5)P2.
source: Comparing the kinetics of PI(4,5)P2 production on SLBs in the presence of either PIP5KB and PIP5KB (D51R) revealed that dimerization enhances catalytic activity, but is not essential for generation of PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Kinetic analysis of PIP5KB (D51R/R254D)-driven lipid phosphorylation showed that restoring the dimer interface through an orthogonal salt bridge produced a kinase with catalytic activity indistinguishable from wild-type PIP5KB.
source: Kinetic analysis of PIP5KB (D51R/R254D)-driven lipid phosphorylation showed that restoring the dimer interface through this orthogonal salt bridge produced a kinase with catalytic activity indistinguishable from wild-type PIP5KB (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Over a broad range of solution concentrations, approximately twofold higher membrane density was observed for mNG-PIP5KB, compared to mNG-PIP5KB (D51R).
source: Over a broad range of solution concentrations, we observed approximately twofold higher membrane density for mNG-PIP5KB, compared to mNG-PIP5KB (D51R) (Figure 5F).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The calculated phosphorylation rate constant for the dimer mutant, PIP5KB (D51R), had a single rate constant of 2.3 × 10–4 lipids/µm2•s per enzyme throughout the observed reaction trajectory.
source: The calculated phosphorylation rate constant for the dimer mutant, PIP5KB (D51R), had a single rate constant of 2.3 × 10–4 lipids/µm2•s per enzyme throughout the observed reaction trajectory.
evidence: This statement is based on calculations from experimental data.

claim: The phosphorylation rate constant for wild-type PIP5KB began with a slow rate and then transitioned to a rate of 2.7 × 10–3 lipids/µm2•s per kinase as the reaction progressed.
source: Conversely, the phosphorylation rate constant for wild-type PIP5KB began with a slow rate and then transitioned to a rate of 2.7 × 10–3 lipids/µm2•s per kinase as the reaction progressed (Figure 5G, see arrows indicating the transition from slow to fast kinetics for wild-type PIP5KB).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Dimerization is predominantly responsible for PIP5K higher-order positive feedback.
source: However, mapping the feedback strength based on the reaction coordinate revealed that dimerization is predominantly responsible for PIP5K higher-order positive feedback.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of experimental data.

claim: In the presence of 50 nM PIP5KB (WT or D51R) and 30 nM DrrA-OCRL, the activity of the D51R dimer mutant was strongly impaired compared to wild-type PIP5KB.
source: In the presence of 50 nM PIP5KB (WT or D51R) and 30 nM DrrA-OCRL, we found that the activity of the D51R dimer mutant was strongly impaired compared to wild-type PIP5KB (Figure 6B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Restoring the PIP5KB dimer interface with a charge reversal mutation, D51R/R254D, allowed reconstitution of bistable compositional patterns that were indistinguishable from those formed in the presence of wild-type PIP5K.
source: Restoring the PIP5KB dimer interface with a charge reversal mutation, D51R/R254D, allowed us to reconstitute bistable compositional patterns that were indistinguishable from those formed in the presence of wild-type PIP5K (Figure 6B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: After a couple of minutes the PI(4,5)P2 compositional patterns generated by PIP5KB (D51R) were consumed by the surrounding 5-phosphatase dominated reaction.
source: However, after a couple of minutes the PI(4,5)P2 compositional patterns generated by PIP5KB (D51R) were consumed by the surrounding 5-phosphatase dominated reaction (Figure 6B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In the presence of mNG-PIP5KB, the kinase membrane density steadily increased and then plateaued shortly after pattern formation.
source: In the presence of mNG-PIP5KB, the kinase membrane density steadily increased and then plateaued shortly after pattern formation (Figure 6D, Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The membrane surface density of mNG-PIP5K (D51R) sharply increased immediately after initiating the kinase–phosphatase competitive reactions, reaching a density nearly two times greater compared to the steady-state density observed for mNG-PIP5KB.
source: In contrast, the membrane surface density of mNG-PIP5K (D51R) sharply increased immediately after initiating the kinase–phosphatase competitive reactions, reaching a density nearly two times greater compared to the steady-state density observed for mNG-PIP5KB (Figure 6D, Figure 6—video 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: PIP5KB reaction trajectories displayed a high degree of kinetic heterogeneity under conditions of geometric confinement.
source: Under these conditions, PIP5KB reaction trajectories displayed a high degree of kinetic heterogeneity (Figure 7A and B, Figure 7—video 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Reactions reconstituted in the presence of PIP5KB (D51R) showed little heterogeneity, confirming that dimerization strongly enhanced variation in corral reaction trajectory.
source: In contrast, reactions reconstituted in the presence of PIP5KB (D51R) showed little heterogeneity, confirming that dimerization strongly enhanced variation in corral reaction trajectory (Figure 7B, Figure 7—video 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Wild-type PIP5KB exhibits a much more robust bistability, which spans a substantially wider range of competing phosphatase concentrations than observed for the PIP5KB (D51R) dimer mutant.
source: Wild-type PIP5KB exhibits a much more robust bistability, which spans a substantially wider range of competing phosphatase concentrations than observed for the PIP5KB (D51R) dimer mutant.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of experimental data.

claim: Dimerization of PIP5K ensures that the kinase–phosphatase-competitive reactions can achieve a bistable response over a broad range of opposing 5-phosphatase activity.
source: Dimerization of PIP5K thus ensures that the kinase–phosphatase-competitive reactions can achieve a bistable response over a broad range of opposing 5-phosphatase activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of experimental data.

claim: Cooperative PI(4,5)P2 binding and membrane-mediated dimerization provide synergistic mechanisms to increase the rate of PI(4,5)P2 production through the enhanced localization and increased catalytic efficiency of PIP5K.
source: Cooperative PI(4,5)P2 binding and membrane-mediated dimerization provide synergistic mechanisms to increase the rate of PI(4,5)P2 production through the enhanced localization and increased catalytic efficiency of PIP5K (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Dimerization enhances PIP5K lipid kinase activity by directly increasing kcat, independent of increasing membrane avidity of PIP5K.
source: Supporting a mechanism of allosteric regulation, our results indicate that dimerization enhances PIP5K lipid kinase activity by directly increasing kcat. This effect is independent of increasing membrane avidity of PIP5K.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of experimental data.

claim: Amos et al. reported that only a single kinase domain can engage substrate when the PIP5K dimer is docked on a PI(4)P-containing membrane.
source: Working under the assumption that PIP5K is constitutively dimeric, Amos et al. reported that only a single kinase domain can engage substrate when the dimer is docked on a PI(4)P-containing membrane.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Membrane-mediated dimerization is expected to enhance processivity of membrane-bound PIP5K by allowing kinase domains to toggle between states of catalysis and membrane binding.
source: If this mechanism is accurate, membrane-mediated dimerization is expected to enhance processivity of membrane-bound PIP5K by allowing kinase domains to toggle between states of catalysis and membrane binding.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on previous work.

claim: This mechanism would ensure that dimeric PIP5K remains bound to the membrane during enzyme catalysis, while the monomeric PIP5K would likely catalyze a single PI(4)P phosphorylation reaction before dissociating.
source: This mechanism would ensure that dimeric PIP5K remains bound to the membrane during enzyme catalysis, while the monomeric PIP5K would likely catalyze a single PI(4)P phosphorylation reaction before dissociating.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the proposed mechanism.

claim: Both subunits of the PIP5K kinase domain can engage the membrane, based on the enhanced dwell time and slower diffusion coefficient observed when Ax647-PIP5K is visualized at high protein density.
source: According to our single-molecule biophysical studies, we believe that both subunits of the PIP5K kinase domain can engage the membrane. This is based on the enhanced dwell time and slower diffusion coefficient observed when Ax647-PIP5K is visualized is high protein density (i.e., ~100 molecules/µm2).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of experimental data.

claim: Cooperative PI(4,5)P2 binding, membrane-mediated dimerization, and low molecular copy number of PIP5K provide several mechanisms for enhancing stochasticity in membrane-associated lipid phosphorylation reactions.
source: Cooperative PI(4,5)P2 binding, membrane-mediated dimerization, and low molecular copy number of PIP5K provide several mechanisms for enhancing stochasticity in membrane-associated lipid phosphorylation reactions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Reaction velocity fluctuations driven by stochastic binding and unbinding of PIP5K on the membrane could drive the system to a predominantly PI(4,5)P2 state, even in the presence of high levels of opposing lipid phosphatase activity.
source: Previously, we reported that reaction velocity fluctuations driven by stochastic binding and unbinding of PIP5K on the membrane could drive the system to a predominantly PI(4,5)P2 state, even in the presence of high levels of opposing lipid phosphatase activity that were sufficient to drive the system predominantly to the PI(4)P state in bulk (Hansen et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Dimerization is responsible for the higher-order positive feedback exhibited by PIP5K, and this contributes to the robustness with which this system exhibits stochastic geometry sensing.
source: Here, we report that dimerization is responsible for the higher-order positive feedback exhibited by PIP5K, and this contributes to the robustness with which this system exhibits stochastic geometry sensing.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: Without dimerization, PIP5K displays a simple linear positive feedback profile.
source: Without dimerization, PIP5K displays a simple linear positive feedback profile.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: Stochasticity in PIP5K signaling has the potential to strongly influence signaling events orchestrated at the plasma membrane in living cells.
source: Given the broad dynamic range of kinase densities and activities that can emerge from these biochemical mechanisms, stochasticity in PIP5K signaling has the potential to strongly influence signaling events orchestrated at the plasma membrane in living cells.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the experimental findings.

claim: Human proteomic data has estimated the cellular concentration of PIP5K in mammalian cells to be 10–20 nM.
source: Human proteomic data has estimated the cellular concentration of PIP5K in mammalian cells to be 10–20 nM (Hein et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Based on the weak monomer–dimer equilibrium, PIP5K is predicted to exist predominantly as a monomer in the cytoplasm.
source: Based on the weak monomer–dimer equilibrium, PIP5K is predicted to exist predominantly as a monomer in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: Receptor activation could shift the steady-state localization of PIP5K to favor membrane-dependent dimerization and enhanced lipid kinase activity.
source: However, receptor activation could shift the steady-state localization of PIP5K to favor membrane-dependent dimerization and enhanced lipid kinase activity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the experimental findings.

claim: PIP5K can reportedly interact with phosphatidylserine and sterol lipids, which modulate lipid kinase activity.
source: Complicating our interpretation of cellular localization, PIP5K can also reportedly interact with phosphatidylserine and sterol lipids, which modulate lipid kinase activity (Nishimura et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: PIP5KA, PIP5KB, and PIP5KC paralogs can potentially form heterodimeric complexes that have unique membrane avidities and kinase activities.
source: In addition, PIP5KA, PIP5KB, and PIP5KC paralogs can potentially form heterodimeric complexes that have unique membrane avidities and kinase activities (Lacalle et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Several basic residues are critical for PIP binding and plasma membrane localization in cells.
source: Previously published cell biology data reported that several basic residues are critical for PIP binding and plasma membrane localization in cells (Fairn et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: These basic residues are dispensable for PIP5K membrane binding and activity in vitro.
source: However, these basic residues are dispensable for PIP5K membrane binding and activity in vitro (Hansen et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: PIP5K becomes enriched at synaptic vesicles and focal adhesions.
source: We know from previous work that PIP5K becomes enriched at synaptic vesicles (Nakano-Kobayashi et al., 2007) and focal adhesions (Ling et al., 2002; Di Paolo et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: It remains unclear whether localization of PIP5K to these cellular structures requires interactions with PI(4,5)P2 lipids, dimerization of the kinase domain, or recruitment by peripheral membrane proteins.
source: However, it remains unclear whether localization of PIP5K to these cellular structure requires interactions with PI(4,5)P2 lipids, dimerization of the kinase domain, or recruitment by peripheral membrane proteins.
